One clear path

Every SQA concept, in the order you need it.

Eight stages from the QA mindset to your first job — each lesson tagged beginner, intermediate or advanced so you always know where you are.

Beginner

The QA mindset, SDLC/STLC, test cases, boundary values, bug reports, web and API basics.

  • What software testing is — and why it matters
  • QA, QC and testing: the tester’s role and mindset
  • Error, defect, failure and the seven testing principles
  • Test activities, testware, traceability and independence
  • SDLC models: Waterfall, V-model, iterative and Agile

23 lessons

Intermediate

Decision tables, exploratory testing, SQL joins, Postman, auth, Playwright, accessibility and security.

  • Test levels and test types
  • Static testing, reviews, and verification vs validation
  • Testing in Agile and Scrum
  • Test-first development: TDD, ATDD and BDD
  • Maintenance testing and impact analysis

38 lessons

Advanced

Risk-based strategy, pairwise testing, contract tests, flaky tests, CI/CD, performance, release decisions.

  • Risk-based testing and building a test strategy
  • Use cases, pairwise and combinatorial testing
  • Test planning, estimation, traceability and reporting
  • Emulators, simulators, real devices and device clouds
  • Usability, localization and internationalization testing

19 lessons

FAQ

Questions, answered.

Quick answers about what Qadence is, what it costs, what you learn and where your progress lives.

What is Qadence?

Qadence is a free, open-source website for learning software testing and quality assurance (QA) step by step, from your first test case to automation, APIs, performance and security. It has 80 lessons in 8 stages, 630 multiple-choice questions, 12 scenario tests, 41 practice drills and 221 interview questions, and it runs entirely in your browser.

Is Qadence free, and do I need an account?

Yes, Qadence is completely free and open source under the MIT License. There is no sign-up: the sign-in screen shows a shared demo login that anyone can use, and it is a simple gate, not a real account.

What will I learn?

You learn software testing in 8 stages: QA foundations, manual testing, web & mobile, SQL & APIs, code & Git, automation & CI, quality breadth and career & capstone. Every lesson is tagged beginner, intermediate or advanced and has a visual guide, a worked example, practice exercises and a 5-question quick check.

Does Qadence help with QA interviews and the ISTQB Foundation exam?

Yes. The lessons are mapped to the ISTQB CTFL v4.0.1 syllabus, and the interview prep has 221 frequently asked questions in 13 topics with model answers, flashcards and mock interviews. Qadence is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by ISTQB.

Which languages does Qadence support?

Lessons are written in English, and every lesson adds a simple explanation in 11 languages: Urdu, Roman Urdu, Hindi, Arabic, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese and Korean. The whole interface can switch to any of these 12 languages, with a right-to-left layout for Urdu and Arabic.

Where is my progress saved?

Only in this browser’s local storage on your device; nothing is sent to a server. Progress does not sync across browsers or devices, and clearing this site’s browser data deletes it, so export a backup from Data & privacy if you want to keep it.

How long does it take to finish?

The full roadmap is planned at about 24 weeks, or roughly 240–288 hours of study at 10–12 hours a week. These are planning estimates, not a promise: go at your own pace, and finishing the course does not guarantee a job.
